Bear’s Sink or Float Lab

Age 4–5 YearsClass 31 · ScienceSkill Predict and test

Wood, metal, cork, stone — guess first, then sort all six objects into the right tubs.

Play the science game ↓Print the worksheet ↓Play with a finger, a stylus or a mouse. Instructions are spoken aloud.
PLAY · PREDICT AND TEST

Bear’s Sink or Float Lab

Bear is testing objects in water! Tap a picture, then tap the tub where you think it belongs. What sinks — and what floats?

Tap a picture, then tap its tub: float or sink?

Lab results are in!

The cork, wooden block and boat float. The metal spoon, key and stone sink!

FOR GROWN-UPS

Why this adventure helps.

Sorting here is only half the fun: drop a spoon and a cork in the bath afterwards and let your child run the real experiment. Ask WHY the heavy-feeling boat still floats.

Illustration note: This is a prediction game: the child sorts first, and the say-lines confirm the real result. The material is the clue — wood and cork float; metal and stone sink.

Prefer paper? The Bear’s Sink or Float Lab worksheet prints the same experiment with room to think and draw — and a grown-up answer line. Printing never marks anything complete.
